rounds.text: Supreme Engineering Ltd is demonstrating powerful underlying earnings acceleration, evidenced by a massive 87% compounded profit growth over the trailing twelve months and a 26% growth rate over three years [E18, E17]. Rules-based screening explicitly flags accelerating earnings, quarterly profit growth, and an astonishing net profit surge of 2029% YoY [E51, E53, E54]. This operational momentum is directly converting into cash, with operating cash flow hitting Rs 1.27 Cr and free cash flow reaching Rs 1.13 Cr in March 2026, representing an exceptional 103% conversion of operating profit [E27, E28, E29]. Market participants are recognizing this fundamental turnaround, sending the stock 280% higher over the past year and placing it firmly at 100% of its 52-week range above both its 50-day and 200-day moving averages [E21, E37, E39]. Furthermore, the company benefits from a powerful macroeconomic backdrop as the Capital Goods sector sits in a verified tailwind with a score of +1.04 [E58, E60]. Conceded: long-term sales growth has contracted by 14% over 10 years and the discounted cash flow model suggests the current price of Rs 3.65 outpaces its strict intrinsic value estimate of Rs 1 [E12, E34].

Supreme Engineering Ltd carries fundamental strains and a stark valuation disconnect that the evidence exposes across multiple dimensions. Compounded sales growth has contracted severely over longer horizons, dropping by -14% over 10 years and -19% over 5 years, accompanied by a -4% contraction in the trailing twelve months and a sharp -52% year-on-year sales drop flagged by the screening engine [E12, E13, E15, E55]. Financial stability is compromised by deeply negative book value of -3.58 resulting in a -1.02x price-to-book ratio, alongside a low interest coverage ratio, negative ROCE figures of 0.8%, and a burdensome debt stack of Rs 104.38 Cr [E1, E11, E30, E48]. Valuation metrics are heavily strained, with an EV/EBITDA of 52.75x towering over the sector benchmark of 13.75x, and a reverse DCF revealing that the current market price already prices in an aggressive 32.2% earnings growth rate [E10, E36]. This rich pricing sits at the absolute peak of its 52-week range following a 272.9% twelve-month return, leaving the stock vulnerable given its historical susceptibility to an 88.0% peak-to-trough drawdown and high annualised volatility of 68.6% [E4, E37, E42, E43, E57]. Conceded: trailing twelve-month profit growth reached 87%, net profit surged 2029% year-on-year, and operating cash flow is positive at Rs 1.27 Cr [E18, E27, E51].

The bear flags long-term sales contraction, but ignores that recent trends show a powerful operational reversal, including 11% 3-year sales growth, 26% 3-year profit growth, and an 87% surge in trailing twelve-month profit [E14, E17, E18]. Conceded: compounded sales growth over 5 years is -19% [E13]. Regarding financial stability, the company generates positive operating cash flow of Rs 1.27 Cr and free cash flow of Rs 1.13 Cr, with cash flow reaching 103% of operating profit [E27, E28, E29]. Furthermore, borrowings ticked down to Rs 104.38 Cr from Rs 104.45 Cr, proving deleveraging is underway [E30]. Conceded: the interest coverage ratio is flagged as low [E48]. On valuation and momentum, the rich metrics and 52-week peak are backed by a rules-based screen score of 70 out of 100 alongside a sector tailwind score of +1.04, placing the business squarely in a supportive macro backdrop [E4, E37, E50, E58]. Finally, the stock trades above its 50-day and 200-day moving averages with a relative-strength rating of 100, validating that market participants are actively rewarding the accelerating earnings profile [E39, E40, E54].

The bull points to recent 3-year sales growth of 11%, 3-year profit growth of 26%, and an 87% trailing profit surge [E14, E17, E18], but glosses over the severe structural decay captured by a 19% 5-year and 14% 10-year compounded sales contraction [E12, E13]. Conceded: the company generates positive operating and free cash flows of Rs 1.27 Cr and Rs 1.13 Cr respectively [E27, E28]. However, this nominal cash generation is entirely undermined by a dangerously heavy debt load of Rs 104.38 Cr that barely moved from the previous year [E30], leaving the business explicitly flagged for a low interest coverage ratio [E48]. While the bull cites sector tailwinds and a score of 70 out of 100 on a rules-based screen [E50, E58], it ignores the glaring internal fundamentals: a dismal 0.8% ROCE [E11], an inconsistent quarterly margin trend that dropped to -1% in June 2026 [E23, E25], and screen alerts highlighting a 52% year-over-year sales collapse [E55]. Finally, the claim that market momentum validates the price ignores the staggering -314.5% margin of safety and a reverse DCF showing the stock aggressively prices in 32.2% growth against a 12% base case [E35, E36], leaving the 100% 52-week peak [E4] dangerously divorced from the underlying reality of extreme volatility [E43] and historical drawdowns of -88% [E42].
